title: Maximum Frequency Stack
description: Brute force to optimized: recomputing frequencies on every pop versus frequency-grouped stacks with O(1) operations.

blocks.text: 1. Problem Statement

Design a stack-like structure supporting push(value) and pop(), where pop always removes and returns the most frequent element currently in the stack. If multiple elements share the same highest frequency, the one that was pushed most recently among them is removed.

blocks.caption: Group elements by their current frequency; each group is its own stack ordered by arrival

blocks.text: 2. Pattern Detection

blocks.text: 3. Understand the Problem

Design a stack-like structure supporting push(value) and pop(), where pop always removes and returns the most frequent element currently in the stack. If multiple elements share the same highest frequency, the one that was pushed most recently among them is removed.

blocks.title: Analogy: Serving the Most Requested Dish, Freshest First
blocks.text: Like a kitchen that serves whichever dish has been ordered the most times so far, and if two dishes are tied for the most orders, serves whichever of those was most recently prepared.

blocks.caption: Pop always removes the most frequent value, ties broken by most recent push

blocks.text: 4. Understand with Examples
Example: push 5, 7, 5, 7, 4, 5, then pop repeatedly

blocks.content: {"headers":["Operation","Result","Why"],"rows":[["pop()","5 (frequency 3, the highest)","5 was pushed 3 times in total, more than 7 (2 times) or 4 (1 time), making it the unique element with the highest frequency"],["pop()","7 (frequency 2, tied with nothing higher after 5 is removed)","With one 5 already removed, 5 and 7 are the two values tied at the highest remaining frequency; 7 arrived at that frequency level more recently, so it is chosen first"],["pop()","5 (frequency 2, remaining after removing one earlier 5)","5 is now the sole value at the current highest frequency, since 7 has already dropped to a lower frequency after being popped in the previous step"],["pop()","4 (frequency 1, the last one left)","Every remaining value is now tied at frequency 1, and 4 is the one remaining at that level, so it is removed last"]]}

blocks.text: Example: push 1, push 1, then pop

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Result","Why"],"rows":[["1 has been pushed twice, frequency 2","the only candidate","With only one distinct value present, it is trivially the most frequent regardless of any tie-break rule"],["pop()","1","The only value present is returned, exactly as expected"]]}

blocks.text: Edge case: every pushed value is distinct
When every value has been pushed exactly once, every element is tied at frequency 1, so pop always removes whichever was pushed most recently, behaving exactly like an ordinary stack in this case.
5. How Should We Think?

Before jumping to any specific structure, notice this problem asks for two things simultaneously on every pop: the current maximum frequency among present values, and, among ties at that frequency, whichever arrived most recently, two separate pieces of information that must both stay instantly accessible.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: A pop needs the maximum frequency currently present, but recomputing that maximum from scratch every time throws away the fact that frequency only ever changes by exactly 1 per operation, on the specific value being pushed or popped.

Observation 2: If every value's current frequency is tracked incrementally, a simple hash map updated by 1 on every push and pop, the maximum frequency can also just be tracked as a running pointer, moving up by 1 whenever a push reaches a new peak, and down by 1 whenever the group at the current peak becomes empty.

Observation 3: Among values tied at the same frequency, "most recently pushed" is exactly what a stack, last-in-first-out order, naturally gives, so grouping values by their current frequency level, each group its own stack, answers the tie-break question with a simple "look at the top" instead of a search.

Observation 4: Since a push only ever increases one value's frequency by exactly 1, that value moves from its old frequency group to a new one, one level higher, and a pop only ever removes from the group at the current max frequency, so both operations touch only a constant number of groups, never all of them.

Whenever a data structure needs "the current max of something, with ties broken by recency," consider grouping by that changing value into parallel stacks, plus a running pointer to the current max group, instead of recomputing the max or the tie-break from scratch.

This same "bucket by a small, incrementally-changing quantity, plus a running pointer to the extreme bucket" technique is what made Top K Frequent Elements' bucket sort and this problem's O(1) operations both possible.
6. Brute Force Solution

Keep every pushed value in a simple ordered list. On every pop, rescan the entire remaining list to recompute each value's current frequency from scratch, find the maximum frequency, and among values with that frequency, remove whichever was pushed most recently.
Step by step algorithm

items: Maintain a list of all currently present values, in push order.
On pop, recompute every remaining value's frequency by rescanning the whole list.
Find the maximum frequency, then scan from the end of the list backward to find the most recent value with that frequency, and remove it.

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: values is kept as a single flat list in push order, since the brute force intentionally avoids any extra bookkeeping structure, recomputing everything fresh on every pop instead.
counts is rebuilt completely from scratch at the start of every pop call, since the brute force has no incrementally maintained frequency information to reuse from any prior operation.

The backward scan, from the end of values toward the start, specifically looks for the last, most recently pushed, value matching the maximum frequency, directly implementing the tie-break rule via array position rather than any separate recency tracking.

blocks.text: 7. Analyze the Brute Force
Every pop correctly identifies the true maximum frequency and the most recently pushed value among ties, so the behavior is correct.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(n) per pop, rescanning and recomputing frequencies from scratch every time.
Space: O(n), for the list of values.

Limitation: recomputing every value's frequency from scratch on every single pop is far more work than necessary, when frequencies could instead be tracked incrementally as values are pushed and popped.
8. Optimize the Solution

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text: The brute force's O(n) per pop comes entirely from rebuilding information, every value's frequency, that barely changed since the last operation: exactly one value's frequency shifted by exactly 1 since the previous push or pop, and everything else stayed identical. Recomputing every value's count from that unchanged state is pure waste. If frequency is instead tracked incrementally, updated by exactly 1 on the one value actually being pushed or popped, then the only remaining question is how to still answer "what is the max, and who is most recent among ties" without a search. Grouping values by their current frequency into separate stacks answers both questions directly: the group index itself tracks max frequency, just move a pointer up or down by 1, and each group's own stack ordering answers the tie-break for free.

Maintain a running frequency count for every value, updated directly on each push. Also maintain a mapping from each frequency value to a stack of elements currently at that exact frequency, in the order they reached it, so the most recently arrived element at any given frequency is always on top of its group's stack. Track the current maximum frequency seen. A push increments the value's frequency, adds it to its new frequency group's stack, and updates the maximum frequency if needed. A pop removes the top of the maximum frequency group's stack, decrements that value's frequency, and if the maximum frequency group becomes empty, decrements the maximum frequency.
9. Optimized Solution
Group elements by their current frequency, each group its own stack ordered by arrival, with a running pointer to the current maximum frequency group.
Dry run for push 5, 7, 5, 7, 4, 5, then pop

blocks.content: {"headers":["Step","Frequency of value","Frequency group stacks","Max frequency","Why"],"rows":[["push 5","5:1","group 1: [5]","1","5 has never been pushed before, so it starts fresh in the frequency-1 group"],["push 7","7:1","group 1: [5, 7]","1","7 also starts fresh at frequency 1, joining 5 in the same group, arriving after it"],["push 5","5:2","group 1: [5, 7], group 2: [5]","2","5's frequency increases from 1 to 2, so this occurrence moves up into a brand new group 2, and max frequency rises to match"],["push 7","7:2","group 1: [5, 7], group 2: [5, 7]","2","7's frequency also increases to 2, joining group 2 after 5, since 7 arrived at this frequency level more recently"],["push 4","4:1","group 1: [5, 7, 4], group 2: [5, 7]","2","4 is brand new, starting at frequency 1 alongside 5 and 7's original group 1 entries; max frequency is unaffected since 4 only reaches level 1"],["push 5","5:3","group 1: [5, 7, 4], group 2: [5, 7], group 3: [5]","3","5's frequency climbs to 3, the highest yet, so a new group 3 is created just for this occurrence, and max frequency rises again"],["pop","-","removes 5 from group 3 (now empty), max frequency drops to 2","returns 5","Group 3 held only this one occurrence of 5; once it is removed, that group is empty, so the max frequency pointer correctly falls back to 2"]]}

blocks.caption: Optimized: elements grouped by current frequency, each group its own stack ordered by arrival

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(1) for both push and pop.
Space: O(n), for the frequency map and the grouped stacks.
Why This Works

Every push moves exactly one occurrence into a new group one level higher than before, and every pop removes exactly one occurrence from the current top group, which is always the group matching the true current maximum frequency, since maxFreq is only ever incremented the moment a push actually reaches a new peak, and only ever decremented the moment the group it points at becomes empty. Because each group is itself a stack, its own top is always whichever occurrence most recently arrived at that specific frequency level, correctly implementing the tie-break rule without ever comparing timestamps directly.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Event","Effect on maxFreq"],"rows":[["A push reaches a frequency strictly greater than the current maxFreq","maxFreq increases to match this new peak"],["A pop empties out the group currently at maxFreq","maxFreq decreases by 1, since the next-highest occupied group is guaranteed to be exactly one level down"]]}

blocks.text: Code walkthrough

items: Computing the new frequency a push reaches determines exactly which group this occurrence belongs to, since that group index is simply the value's updated frequency.
Each push always appends onto the end of its target group's list, so the most recently arrived occurrence at that frequency level is always the last element, ready to be popped first.
maxFreq only ever grows during a push, since a push can only ever increase some value's frequency, never decrease the overall maximum.
maxFreq only ever shrinks inside pop, and only when the group just popped from becomes completely empty, correctly reflecting that the current peak group no longer holds anything.

blocks.text: 10. Complexity Comparison

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","Time","Space","Notes"],"rows":[["Brute force (rescan and recompute on every pop)","O(n) per pop","O(n)","Every pop rebuilds every value's frequency from scratch before finding the max and the tie-break"],["Optimized (frequency-grouped stacks with a max pointer)","O(1) per operation","O(n)","Both push and pop touch only a constant number of groups, with the max frequency tracked incrementally"]]}

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

The core insight is grouping elements by their current frequency in separate stacks, so both "find the max frequency" and "find the most recent among ties" become O(1) lookups, rather than needing to recompute anything.
Common mistakes

items: Forgetting to decrement maxFreq when its group empties out, which would cause future pops to look in the wrong, now-empty group and fail instead of finding the true next-highest group.

Using a single shared list per frequency without preserving arrival order, which breaks the "most recent among ties" rule, since the tie-break specifically depends on which occurrence arrived at that frequency level last.
Assuming maxFreq might need to search downward more than one level when a group empties, when it can only ever need to drop by exactly 1, since frequencies change by exactly 1 per operation.

blocks.text: Edge cases

blocks.content: {"headers":["Edge case","Expected behavior"],"rows":[["Popping down to a single remaining value","Correctly settles at frequency 1 in group 1, since every other occurrence has already been removed"],["Pushing the same value many times in a row","Keeps climbing to higher and higher frequency groups, one new group per push, since each push increases that value's own frequency by exactly 1"]]}

blocks.text: Interview tips

items: Draw the frequency groups as a set of parallel stacks, and point out that the maxFreq pointer only ever needs to move up on push or down on pop, never search, since it directly tracks the currently highest occupied group.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: "Track the max or min of something dynamically, with ties broken by recency or another secondary rule" points toward grouping elements by that changing quantity into parallel stacks or lists, plus a running pointer to the current extreme group, instead of recomputing or searching.
Interview Follow-up Questions

items: How would you support a "peek" operation that returns, without removing, the value pop would return? Simply read the top of the current max-frequency group's stack without popping it or updating any frequency counts.

What if ties needed to be broken by least recently pushed instead of most recently? Use a queue instead of a stack for each frequency group, so the earliest arrival at that frequency level is served first instead of the latest.

How would you extend this to also support removing an arbitrary specific value, not just the current max-frequency one? That value's entry would need to be locatable and removable from whichever group it currently sits in, typically requiring each group to be a more flexible structure, like a doubly linked list, supporting O(1) arbitrary removal, not just a plain stack.

blocks.text: Pattern Connections

items: Same "bucket by a changing quantity, track a running pointer to the extreme" technique as Top K Frequent Elements and Sort Characters By Frequency's bucket sort by frequency.
Same "stack per group gives free most-recent tie-breaking" idea reusable in any "max or min with ties broken by recency" design problem.
Same incremental frequency tracking, a hash map updated by exactly 1 per operation, as LFU Cache's frequency bookkeeping, one level more advanced.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text:
Brute force: O(n) time per pop, O(n) space.
Optimized (frequency grouped stacks): O(1) time per operation, O(n) space.
12. Final Summary

items: Pattern: Frequency-grouped stacks with a running pointer to the current maximum frequency group
Core Idea: Group elements by their current frequency into separate stacks, so the max frequency is tracked by a pointer and ties are broken automatically by each group's own stack order
Time: O(1) for both push and pop
Space: O(n)

Most Important Observation: A quantity that only changes by exactly 1 per operation, like a frequency count or a running maximum, never needs to be recomputed from scratch, only incrementally adjusted
Interview Difficulty: Hard
One-line memory trick: One stack per frequency level, max pointer moves by exactly 1
